tutorial.title: Environmental Acoustic Intelligence
tutorial.subtitle: From Acoustic Perception towards Context-Aware Sound Intervention
tutorial.arc: Perception → Contextual Understanding → Context-Aware Action → Purposeful Sound Intervention

presenters_line: Prof. Woon-Seng Gan · Dr. Ee-Leng Tan · Mr. Jun-Wei Yeow (NTU Singapore)

lab.name: Smart Nation TRANS Lab
lab.school: School of Electrical and Electronic Engineering

abstract.text: Environmental Acoustic Intelligence moves from sensing acoustic environments towards understanding them and supporting purposeful intervention. The tutorial follows the progression Hear → Understand → Reason → Act. It begins with spatial perception through Sound Event Localization and Detection (SELD), including scalable data-centric learning and language interfaces that broaden spatial acoustic information. It then combines Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC), Sound Event Detection (SED), and SELD to turn scene, event, and spatial cues into Contextual Understanding. The second half addresses Context-Aware Action: AI-assisted Active Noise Control for practical acoustic challenges, Soundscape Augmentation beyond noise reduction, and Intelligent Sound Management for hearables. Together, these directions extend intervention towards adaptive, human-aware systems that listen with understanding and act with purpose.

items: Explain how Sound Event Localization and Detection (SELD) builds spatial acoustic perception by identifying what happens, when it happens, and where it occurs.
Describe the modern SELD pipeline and the data-centric and language-enabled developments that broaden spatial perception.
Explain how Acoustic Scene Classification (ASC), Sound Event Detection (SED), and SELD integrate to form Contextual Understanding.
Discuss how AI-assisted Active Noise Control addresses nonlinearity, slow adaptation, acoustic-path variation, and generalization.
Explain how Soundscape Augmentation moves beyond noise reduction towards positive acoustic environments.
Discuss Intelligent Sound Management for hearables as a programmable, adaptive, and human-aware form of Context-Aware Action.
